To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the encapsulation in alginate or in protein matrices protected B. animalis subsp lactis Bb 12 against the conditions of a simulated GIT.
co encapsulation in protein matrix with inulin and/or vitamin C is an efficient way of protection of Bifidum animalis Bb12 cells against the conditions of a GIT.
the co encapsulation with both inulin and asccorbic acid in milk protein matrix was the most efficient for Bb12 cells survival in a model GIT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility to protect Bb12 cells from the conditions of GIT using different types of encapsulation with inuline and ascorbic acids.
the development of novel encapsulation technologies of Bb12 with the use of milk protein matrix or alginate matrix.
the influence of co encapsulating Bb12 cells with inulin and/or L ascorbic acid in protein or alginate matrices on its resistance to the conditions of GIT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

both types of capsules with co encapsulated inulin and as corbic acid were effective in protecting Bb12 cells against in vitro GIT conditions, and that alginate and protein matrices were equally efficient in this respect.
both types of capsules (protein or alginate) are effective for the protection of B. animalis subsp lactis Bb 12 cells during the GIT passage.
encapsulation of Bb12 in protein matrix with addition of inuline (1% w w) and ascorbic acid (0. 5% w w) provided the best protection of Bb12 against the conditions of a simulated GIT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the encapsulation of bifidobacteria in alginate matrix with addition of inuline and ascorbic acids is a suitable method for the protection of Bb12 against the conditions of GIT.

the most suitable type of capsule for Bb12 cells would be protein capsules with addition of 1% w/ w inulin and 1% w/v ascorbic acid, which provide the highest viability of cells after exposure to conditions of a model GIT.
co encapsulation with 1% of inulin and 1% of ascorbic acid in milk protein matrix is the most efficient method to protect the viability of probiotics in GIT.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of inulin and asco rbic acid in the co encapsulation with Bb12 in milk protein matrix may be a useful approach to improve the survival of probiotic bacteria during the passage through the GIT and thus to increase the efficacy of the probiotic products.
encapsulation of probiotic bacteria is a promising approach for improving probiotic viability and stability in GIT.

the co encapsulation of probiotic B. animalis subsp lactis Bb 12 with inulin (0.5 1%) and ascorbic (0.5%) acids in protein matrix can improve the resistance of probiotic cells to the conditions in the GIT and may be used in the preparation of probiotic foods.
